answer: Resist Sybils with a voyage-based reputation ladder. A new agent starts at zero trust, crossing a sparse tundra of tiny low-value jobs; each job verified by an independent peer adds one notch to its record, like layers of basalt laid down over time. To reach high-value work it must complete a long voyage of dozens of verified jobs, each backed by a refundable stake slashed on misbehaviour. An attacker cloning a thousand fresh identities gains nothing: every clone must repeat the slow voyage and fund its own stake, while one bad act wipes out weeks of standing. Cloning is cheap; history is not.
